about: The evaluation behind "Link in the text": how the model should refer to sources. Each question is answered from the same sources in three schemes: source-numbers, the engine's frame (SAFETY_FRAME_LINKS: link words by the source's number, [words](n)); reference-numbers, the frame it replaced (the same by a Markdown reference, [words][n], which a deployed check saw the model finish with definitions numbered its own way, [1]: https://…); and copied-addresses, the frame changed to ask for the sources' addresses copied into the link ([words](url)). Each answer is put through the engine's link rules and counted as linked correctly, linked nothing, or had a link removed, and as linking the expected page when at least one of its links goes to a page in the case's `expect` (for the written-answer case, whose `expect` is empty: when it links nothing). `referenceStyle` counts, over `answers` and `samples` (further answers to the same requests), the answers that wrote a [words][n] link or a definition. The solv.chat pages are sections of this repository's docs/architecture.md under stand-in addresses; the sqlite-commercial case is the deployed check's question over excerpts of sqlite.org pages, retrieved in the order that check numbered them. The open-source case's only fitting source is a written answer, which must get no link. Replayed by test/chat/sourceLinksEval.test.ts; recorded with scripts/source-links-eval.mjs.

widget.title: Install the chat widget
widget.text:
A custom element, `<solv-chat assistant="pk_...">`, loaded with one script tag.
No framework, no dependencies, Shadow DOM, one file, under 30 kB gzipped.
Streams tokens, renders citations as links, restores the open conversation after a
page change or reload (conversation id, transcript and open state in sessionStorage,
so it ends with the tab), thumbs up and down, keyboard and
screen-reader usable, respects `prefers-reduced-motion` and `prefers-color-scheme`.
It sets no cookies and loads nothing from third parties into the host page:
with the visitor check on, Turnstile runs inside a frame served by the
engine's origin, created only once the visitor starts typing (see "Visitor
check").

Links in an answer's text (http and https only) open as the source links
under an answer do: `target="_blank"`, `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, and a
link to a page on the host site is no different, also with page help on
(the widget never handles the click; only the `navigate` action moves the
visitor's own page). While an answer streams, a link at the end of the text
that is not complete yet (`[words`, `[words]`, `[words](https://…`) is held
back until it is, then shown as a link; once the stream ends everything that
arrived is shown. The engine sends links whole anyway (see "Sources in
answers").

page-actions.title: Page actions
page-actions.text:
The assistant can act inside the page the visitor is on, not only answer. Asked
"how do I change my plan?", it can take the visitor to the billing section and
point at the control; asked to "book a demo for Tuesday", it can fill the form
and leave the visitor to press Submit.

Actions run in the visitor's browser, with the visitor's own session. No owner
credential is involved, which makes them safer than MCP tools.

Built in:

- `navigate` — go to a URL on the same site (same origin, or an origin the owner
  listed), optionally to a section:
  - Same-document target (only the fragment differs, or the current URL with a
    section): scrolls to the section and continues the conversation in place.
  - Same-origin target: persists the pending continuation in per-origin
    `sessionStorage` and calls `location.assign`; the next page's widget resumes
    the conversation on connect (dropped as "the visitor moved on" if the
    visitor sends a new message first or after 2 minutes).
  - Listed other origin: keeps the conversation on the current page and renders
    a button ("Open <host> in a new tab") that opens the owner's URL with
    `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"` on click, without passing
    any transcript, ids, or extra parameters.
  - Any other origin: refused.
- `highlight` — scroll to an element and point at it with a short note.
- `fill` — put values into form fields the owner has marked as fillable. It never
  submits.

answering.title: How answers are made
answering.text:
1. Load the published version (or the draft, for the admin "Try it" pane).
2. Retrieve: embed the question, query the retriever for the assistant for 20
   candidates (`CANDIDATE_POOL`; Vectorize returns up to 100 without values or
   metadata). When some hits have no chunk (the index has not caught up; see
   "Index lag") and the index may hold more above the floor (the query came
   back full and its last hit cleared it), it is queried once more, with the
   same org and assistant filters, for 100 (`REFILL_TOP_K`), and the pool is
   the best 20 live candidates of both, resolved together so a current chunk
   of a page leaves out its replaced chunks whichever query returned them.
   Never more than two queries; the cost is one more vector query and one
   more D1 read (of both queries' hits), only on answers that met
   stale hits, and it is counted in the trace's retrieval time. Then give
   the model at most 6 (`TOP_K`) above a score floor
   (0.2), chosen by `selectCandidates` (below). The floor only keeps out
   unrelated content: the model already declines when given content that does
   not hold the answer. Measured with `text-embedding-3-small` against short
   owner-written answers, answerable questions scored 0.25 to 0.43 and unrelated
   ones about 0, so 0.2 sits in the gap (v1's 0.3 refused answerable questions;
   OpenAI documents no absolute threshold). A chunk up to 0.05 under the floor
   is kept too, but only when a chunk of the same document cleared it; when
   nothing clears the floor nothing is kept, so off-topic questions still find
   nothing. An instance may set `SOLV_SCORE_FLOOR` (0 to 0.9); the trace records
   the floor used. Of the chunks that pass the floor, in order:
   - Duplicates: of chunks with the same text under the same title and

answer-tests.title: Answer tests
answer-tests.text:
An owner writes down questions the assistant must keep getting right. A test is
a question plus one expectation: the answer cites a given URL, contains a
phrase, does not contain a phrase, or declines (uses the fallback). "Cites" passes when
the answer links to the URL in its text, or the URL is in its list of sources
(when one is shown) or among the pages it used (when none is), whatever "Show
sources in answers" is (see "Sources in answers").

- Tests run against the draft, through the same pipeline as "Try it": no
  conversation is stored and usage is metered. Each answer's trace is kept in
  `preview_traces`, marked with the run and test, and its id is on the
  result (`traceId`; see "Answer traces").
- Publish runs them first. If any fail, the owner sees which and why, and can
  fix the draft or publish anyway; the choice is recorded on the run.
- `solv test` runs them from CI with the ingest key and exits non-zero on a
  failure. Tests can be declared in `solv.config.json`.
- Conversations and Gaps offer "Add to tests" on any exchange.
- A run is capped (number of tests, wall time) so one click cannot spend
  without limit.

providers.title: Model providers
providers.text:
`LlmProvider` has three implementations: Anthropic, OpenAI and OpenRouter. `Embedder` has two:
OpenAI embeddings (default) and OpenRouter embeddings (`SOLV_EMBEDDINGS_PROVIDER=openrouter`,
fixed to `openai/text-embedding-3-small` at 1536 dimensions). `Retriever` has one: Vectorize; the interface exists so
Cloudflare AI Search can be added as a second backend.

A request may ask for `reasoning: "off"` (the answer review does; visitor
answers do not, and send no reasoning field: only their output limit
leaves room for reasoning, under "Answering a message"). Each provider sends its
own switch: Anthropic `thinking: {type: "disabled"}`, or `{type:
"between_tools"}` on Claude Sonnet 5.5, and nothing on models whose thinking
is always on (Opus 5.5, Fable, Mythos); OpenAI and OpenRouter `reasoning:
{effort: "none"}`. A model that refuses the switch (HTTP 400) is asked once
more without it and with an output limit of at least
`REASONING_FALLBACK_MIN_OUTPUT_TOKENS`, since on every provider reasoning
counts against the output limit; the provider instance then skips the switch
(`providers/reasoning.ts`). A reply that reasoned and then wrote no text and
called no tool is not a successful empty answer: the provider reports its
usage and throws `EmptyReplyError` (a retryable `ProviderError`).

Model IDs, prices and limits live in one file, `packages/engine/src/models.ts`.
Every value in that file is taken from the provider's current documentation and
carries a comment with the source URL and the date checked. Never fill it from
memory.

The admin does not expose model or temperature pickers per assistant. The
instance picks a provider and a model tier in configuration via plain Worker
environment variables (`vars` in `wrangler.jsonc`):

privacy.title: Privacy and retention
privacy.text:
- Conversations and their messages are kept until they are deleted; the open
  engine has no automatic expiry. Deleting a conversation (or its assistant)
  deletes its messages, and with them their feedback, linked gap answers and
  answer traces, by foreign-key cascade.
- A trace adds no visitor or owner text to what is stored: ids, scores,
  timings, a model id and a key source. It is read only by the signed-in
  owner of the org (`/api/admin/*`, org from the auth seam).
- The answer review sends the visitor's question, the assistant's reply, the
  assistant's name, widget title and up to 20 content titles, and the
  assistant's topic names, and nothing else (no conversation history, content
  text, persona, page or visitor id), to
  the same provider that produced the answer, with the same key: the fast
  tier of the organisation's configured answering provider. It stores only
  the label (and a confidence when one is given) and a checked topic name
  (see "Topics"), never the rest of the reviewer's text.
- There is no export of conversations today. Whatever export or deletion path
  is added for messages must cover `message_traces` with them.
- `preview_traces` holds the same ids and numbers for the owner's own "Try
  it" and test-run answers: the newest 200 per assistant, deleted with it.
- The visitor check stores no Turnstile token, session or IP with
  conversations: `visitor_check_tokens` holds token hashes for five minutes
  and `visitor_counters` keyed hashes of visitor ids and IPs for about a day
  (see "Visitor check").

mcp-tools.title: Tools over MCP
mcp-tools.text:
Owners add an MCP server by URL (Streamable HTTP). The Worker lists its tools and
stores them with `allowed = false`. Nothing is callable until the owner switches
a tool on (`allowed = true`) **and** publishes a version whose `allowedTools`
includes it (the "Try it" pane uses the draft's `allowedTools`).

Every visitor is anonymous, and every tool call runs with the owner's
credential. The rules that follow from that:

- Tools are off by default, per tool.
- The admin shows a standing warning that visitors act with this credential and
  recommends a read-only token.
- v1 auth is `none` or a static header. The secret is encrypted with a key from
  a Worker secret (`SOLV_SECRET_KEY`, AES-GCM), decrypted only inside the Worker at
  call time, and never returned by any API — the admin shows "set" or "not set".
- Tool results are untrusted input. They are passed to the model as data, never
  concatenated into the system prompt, and are capped in size.
- Per-conversation caps on the number of tool calls and on wall time.
- Server URLs must be https and must not resolve to private or loopback ranges.

### Conversation context headers

Because every call comes from the Worker, a server cannot tell visitors apart,
so one visitor could use up a budget the server shares between all of them.
Each server has a "Send conversation context" setting (`sendConversationContext`
in the admin API and `solv.config.json`, `send_conversation_context` in D1),
off for existing and new servers. It belongs to the server, not to a version:
it takes effect when saved and Publish does not gate it. When it is on, every
request the engine makes to that server for a chat turn (`initialize`,
`notifications/initialized`, `tools/list` when listed, and `tools/call`)
carries:

visitor-check.title: The visitor check
visitor-check.text:
Nothing else proves that a chat request comes from a real browser on the
owner's page: a script can set `Origin`, and rotating addresses beats the
per-IP rate limit, so a script could use up an assistant's daily spend cap
and lock real visitors out. When an instance is configured for it, every
visitor's browser passes Cloudflare Turnstile and the engine issues a signed
session that public requests must carry.

**Configuration.** `SOLV_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY` (a variable) and
`SOLV_TURNSTILE_SECRET` (a secret), read through the optional
`VisitorCheckProvider` seam (below). Neither set: the check is off and the
public chat behaves exactly as before; the admin shows a standing warning
that visitor chat is unprotected. One set, or both without `SOLV_SECRET_KEY`
to sign sessions with: the public chat refuses every request with
`check_config` ("This chat is not set up correctly.") and the admin names
what is missing. There is no per-assistant switch. Turnstile's documented
test keys work and are flagged: the admin warns that they let everyone
through.

config-as-code.title: Config as code
config-as-code.text:
`solv.config.json` in a site's repository describes an assistant's behaviour,
widget and tests. `solv apply` writes the draft with the ingest key
(`SOLV_INGEST_KEY`); publishing always happens in the admin. `solv push` sends
content; `solv test` runs the tests. The admin and the file edit the same draft.
A `tests` array in `solv.config.json` **replaces** the assistant's stored tests
rather than merging with them. An `mcpServers` array
(`[{ "url", "sendConversationContext" }]`) sets "Send conversation context" on
servers already added in the admin, matched by url; the file cannot add a
server, because its credential has no place in a repository. Through the ingest
key it can turn the setting off but not on (see "Conversation context
headers"), and `solv apply` checks `mcpServers` with a dry run before writing
anything, so a refused entry leaves the draft, tests and servers unchanged.
Because an ingest key can change an assistant's draft behaviour as well as its
content, it must be kept as a secret.

sitemap-sync.title: Scheduled sitemap sync
sitemap-sync.text:
A sitemap source can stay in step with its sitemap. Its `sync` setting is
`off` (the default, so sources created before this existed do not change),
`daily` or `weekly`. A run:

1. Takes the source's lease (`source_syncs.lease_until`, 6 hours) in one
   statement, so two runs of one source never overlap: a cron firing twice,
   or a host's cron beside the open one, starts one run. A run still
   unfinished when its lease ends is reported as `failed` with
   `interrupted`, and its late queue messages change nothing. That holds for
   a page already being fetched when the lease ends: the run is checked again
   after the fetch, and each write a page makes (the document, its
   validators, the page's state, the run's end) carries the same check in its
   own statement.
2. Asks `Limits.checkSync`. A refusal records the run as failed
   (`limit_refused`) and fetches nothing. The org itself was first passed to
   `AuthProvider.resolveOrg` (`queued_ingest`); an org it refuses is not read.
3. Reads the sitemap (the preview's guards and its 2 MiB cap; up to 50,000
   `<url>` entries with their `<lastmod>`). A sitemap index is not followed:
   the run fails with `sitemap_index` ("This is a sitemap index; use one of
   the sitemaps it lists."), and the admin's preview answers 400 with
   `code: "sitemap_index"` rather than listing the child sitemaps as pages.
   Entries are read from the same reading of the XML that step 4 checks, so a
   commented-out `<url>` or `<loc>` is not a listed page.
4.

reports.title: Reports
reports.text:
The Reports screen answers "is it working?" over a date range the owner picks
(7, 30 or 90 days): questions asked, share answered, share with a thumbs down,
cost, response time, the topics, the most asked questions, the most frequent
unanswered questions, and the content used most and never. Everything is
computed from stored rows; the table can be downloaded as CSV.

"Content used most" and "Content never used" count by document id: a reply
used a document when it was given it to answer from (the same chunks its
citations come from), recorded in `message_documents`. Written answers count
as pages do; one is listed by its question, with a link to Sources instead of
an address (the CSV gives its Sources address and the type "Written answer").
A reply counts a document once. Only visitor answers count; "Try it" and test
runs store no message. Replies written before migration 0029 have no record:
for them the URLs in their citations are matched to the assistant's
documents, as before, so older periods count pages but not written answers
(and list a written answer used then as never used). A deleted document is in
neither list, for any period.

The Topics list is the period's visitor questions grouped by topic, most
asked first: each topic, its questions, and the share that could not be
answered (the reply reviewed as `declined`, or unreviewed with no content
found, as Gaps counts one). Each opens Conversations filtered to the topic
for the period. "Most often unanswered" shows each question's topic (that of
its latest tagged ask in the period) as a label. Both are in the CSV.

topics.title: Topics
topics.text:
Top questions are grouped by their exact lowercased text, so "when are you
open" and "opening hours?" are separate rows. Topics group them by what they
are about.

- **Who names them.** The answer review, in the same call (one call, not
  two): it is given the assistant's current topic names and must pick one or
  propose a new short label (2-4 words, at most 40 characters, in the language
  of the question). The topic is stored on the visitor's question (the `user`
  message), not the reply: it describes what was asked, the Topics list
  counts questions, and the Conversations filter finds where it was asked. A
  retrieval miss's question gets one too (its topic stands even when its label
  is replaced by `declined`). An `off_topic` question gets no topic and never
  creates one: it is not about the site, so it would only fill the Topics
  list and the topic filter; the "Off topic" filter is how the owner finds
  these. Migration 0031 cleared the topic of questions tagged before this
  (it keeps every topic: the schema cannot tell an owner-renamed topic from
  one the review named, so one left with no questions stays until the owner
  deletes it). When an answer is stored as `off_topic`, its question's topic
  is cleared first (unless the answer already has another outcome): an
  earlier run may have stored the topic and been cut off before the outcome,
  and the catch-up then finds the question tagged. A question is tagged
  once; nothing re-tags it.
  There is no manual tagging of a message.
- **The cap.** At most 40 topics per assistant (`MAX_TOPICS_PER_ASSISTANT`),
  not counting "Other", which is always available.

open-core.title: Open core and cloud
open-core.text:
| Lives here (Apache 2.0)            | Lives in the closed cloud repo   |
| ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| Chat engine, retrieval, MCP client | Sign-up and login for the public |
| Embeddable widget                  | Teams and roles                  |
| Ingest CLI and GitHub Action       | Billing and usage metering       |
| Multi-assistant admin              | Managed model keys               |

The engine must run complete for a self-hoster with their own provider keys.
The cloud layer plugs in through the seams listed under "Extension seams"; it
never forks engine code.

entry-open-source.title: Is solv.chat open source?
entry-open-source.text: Yes. The chat engine, the widget, the ingest CLI and the admin are open source under the Apache 2.0 licence. Sign-up, teams, billing and managed model keys are part of the hosted service.

sqlite-about.title: About SQLite
sqlite-about.text: SQLite is an in-process library that implements a self-contained, serverless, zero-configuration, transactional SQL database engine. The code for SQLite is in the public domain and is thus free for use for any purpose, commercial or private. SQLite is the most widely deployed database in the world with more applications than we can count, including several high-profile projects.

sqlite-copyright.title: SQLite Copyright
sqlite-copyright.text: All of the code and documentation in SQLite has been dedicated to the public domain by the authors. All code authors, and representatives of the companies they work for, have signed affidavits dedicating their contributions to the public domain and originals of those signed affidavits are stored in a firesafe at the main offices of Hwaci. Anyone is free to copy, modify, publish, use, compile, sell, or distribute the original SQLite code, either in source code form or as a compiled binary, for any purpose, commercial or non-commercial, and by any means.

sqlite-copyright-warranty.title: SQLite Copyright
sqlite-copyright-warranty.headingPath: SQLite Is Public Domain > Warranty of Title
sqlite-copyright-warranty.text: SQLite is in the public domain and does not require a license. Even so, some organizations want legal proof of their right to use SQLite. Circumstances where this occurs include the following: your company desires indemnity against claims of copyright infringement; you are using SQLite in a jurisdiction that does not recognize the public domain. If any of the above circumstances apply to you, Hwaci, the company that employs all the developers of SQLite, will sell you a Warranty of Title for SQLite.

sqlite-faq.title: SQLite Frequently Asked Questions
sqlite-faq.headingPath: Can I use SQLite in my commercial product without paying royalties?
sqlite-faq.text: Yes. SQLite is in the public domain. No claim of ownership is made to any part of the code. You can do anything you want with it.

sqlite-support.title: SQLite Support Options
sqlite-support.text: If you would like professional support for SQLite or if you want custom modifications performed by the original author of SQLite, these services are available for a modest fee. The core SQLite library found on this website is in the public domain. But there also exist proprietary, licensed extensions to SQLite.

cases.question: How do I add the chat to my website?

Load the widget with one script tag, then put the custom element on your page with your assistant's public key:

```html
<solv-chat assistant="pk_..."></solv-chat>
```

It needs no framework and no dependencies, sets no cookies, and is a single file under 30 kB gzipped. It also keeps the conversation going across page changes and reloads. The rest of the setup is on [the chat widget page](1).

cases.question: Can the assistant fill in a form for my visitors?

answers.source-numbers:
Yes. With [page actions](1), the assistant can fill in form fields for a visitor, for example to book a demo. It only fills fields you have marked as fillable, and it never submits the form: the visitor presses Submit themselves.

It can also take the visitor to the right section of a page and point at a control. These actions run in the visitor's own browser session, so no owner credential is involved.

cases.question: What happens when my content does not have the answer to a question?

answers.source-numbers:
The assistant says it does not know rather than guessing. It only gets content that scores above a relevance floor, and when nothing clears it, nothing is passed on, so an off-topic or unanswered question finds nothing. You can read more about this in [how answers are made](1).

Those questions are not lost. [Reports](3) shows the share of questions that could not be answered and lists the most often unanswered ones, so you can see which content to add.
answers.reference-numbers:
The assistant says it does not know rather than guessing. Content that does not hold the answer is not used to make one up.

You can see these cases in [Reports][3], which lists the most frequent unanswered questions and the share of questions that could not be answered, so you know what content to add.
answers.copied-addresses:
The assistant says it does not know rather than guessing. When nothing in your content is close enough to the question, nothing is handed to the model to answer from.

You can find these questions afterwards on the [Reports screen](https://docs.solv.chat/reports), which lists the most often unanswered questions and the share that could not be answered. That shows you which content to add.

cases.question: How can I check the assistant still points to my pricing page before I publish?

answers.source-numbers:
Add an [answer test](1): a question such as "How much does it cost?" with the expectation that the answer cites your pricing page URL. A "cites" test passes when the answer links to that URL, or when the page is among the sources it used.

Publish runs your tests first. If one fails, you see which and why, and you can fix the draft or publish anyway. You can also run the same tests from CI with `solv test`, which exits non-zero on a failure, and the tests can live in `solv.config.json`.
answers.reference-numbers:
Add an answer test for it. A test is a question plus one expectation, and one of the expectations is that the answer cites a given URL. Write a pricing question and expect your pricing page's URL.

```json
{ "question": "How much does it cost?", "expect": "cites", "url": "https://example.com/pricing" }
```

The check passes when the answer links to that URL or the page is among those it used. [Answer tests][1] run automatically when you publish. If any fail, you see which and why, and can fix the draft or publish anyway. You can also run them from CI with `solv test`.
answers.copied-addresses:
Add an [answer test](https://docs.solv.chat/answer-tests) for it: write the question a visitor would ask about pricing and set the expectation that the answer cites your pricing page URL. The test passes when the answer links to that URL or uses that page.

Publishing runs your tests first. If one fails, you see which and why, and you can fix the draft or publish anyway. You can also run them from CI with `solv test`, which exits with an error when a test fails.

You pick one provider and a model tier for the whole instance in its configuration, not per assistant. See [model providers](1) for the details.

cases.question: Can I let the assistant call my own API?

answers.source-numbers:
Yes, by adding an MCP server that exposes your API. You add it by URL (it must be https) in the admin, and its tools are listed but all switched off. A tool can only be called once you turn it on and publish a version that allows it. See [tools over MCP](1) for the rules.

Keep in mind that every visitor is anonymous and every tool call runs with your credential, so use a read-only token. The secret is stored encrypted and is never returned by any API. Tool results are treated as data, are capped in size, and each conversation has limits on the number of calls and on time.
answers.reference-numbers:
Yes. You can add your own MCP server by its URL (it must be https), and the assistant can call its tools. Every tool starts switched off. You turn on the ones you want and publish a version that allows them.

Every visitor is anonymous and each call runs with your credential, so use a read-only token. Details are on [the MCP tools page][1].

If you only need the assistant to act inside your page, such as moving to a section or filling a form, [page actions][2] run in the visitor's own browser and involve no owner credential.
answers.copied-addresses:

cases.question: How do I stop bots from flooding the chat?

answers.source-numbers:
Turn on the [visitor check](1). Every visitor's browser then passes Cloudflare Turnstile, and the engine issues a signed session that public chat requests must carry. Without it, a script can fake the origin and rotate addresses to use up your daily spend cap.

To set it up, set `SOLV_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY` (a variable) and `SOLV_TURNSTILE_SECRET` (a secret), together with `SOLV_SECRET_KEY` to sign sessions. If neither Turnstile value is set, the check is off and the admin warns that visitor chat is unprotected. If only one is set, or the signing key is missing, the chat refuses every request. It applies to the whole instance, not per assistant.
answers.reference-numbers:
Turn on the visitor check. Every visitor's browser then passes Cloudflare Turnstile, and the engine gives it a signed session that chat requests must carry. Scripts that skip this cannot use up your daily spend cap or lock real visitors out.

Set `SOLV_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY` as a variable and `SOLV_TURNSTILE_SECRET` as a secret, and also set `SOLV_SECRET_KEY` so sessions can be signed. With neither Turnstile value set, the check is off and the admin warns that chat is unprotected. See [the visitor check][1] for the full setup.

The check does not store a token, session or IP with conversations. The widget starts it only once the visitor begins typing.

cases.question: Can I keep the assistant's settings in a file in my repository?

answers.source-numbers:
Yes. Put a `solv.config.json` in your repository to describe the assistant's behaviour, widget and tests. [Config as code](1) works like this:

```sh
solv apply   # writes the draft, using SOLV_INGEST_KEY
solv push    # sends content
solv test    # runs the tests
```

Publishing always happens in the admin, and the file and the admin edit the same draft. A `tests` array in the file replaces the stored tests rather than merging with them. The file cannot add an MCP server, because its credential does not belong in a repository. Keep your ingest key secret, since it can change the assistant's draft.
answers.reference-numbers:
Yes. Put a `solv.config.json` in your repository. It describes the assistant's behaviour, widget and tests. Run `solv apply` with your ingest key (`SOLV_INGEST_KEY`) to write it to the draft. Publishing is always done in the admin.

Keep the ingest key secret, because it can change the draft's behaviour as well as its content. A `tests` array in the file replaces the stored tests rather than merging with them. See [config as code][1] for the rest.

cases.question: Will new pages in my sitemap be picked up on their own?

answers.source-numbers:
Only if you turn it on. A sitemap source has a `sync` setting that is `off` by default, so you need to set it to `daily` or `weekly`. Each run then reads the sitemap again and picks up what changed. See [scheduled sitemap sync](1).

One limit: a sitemap index is not followed. The run fails with a message to use one of the sitemaps it lists.
answers.reference-numbers:
Yes, if you turn it on. A sitemap source has a `sync` setting that is `off` by default. Set it to `daily` or `weekly` and the source is re-read on that schedule. Note that a sitemap index is not followed: the run fails, and you need to use one of the sitemaps it lists.

See [scheduled sitemap sync][1] for how a run works.
answers.copied-addresses:

A sitemap index is not followed. Point the source at one of the sitemaps it lists instead.

cases.question: Where do I see which of my pages answers use most?

answers.source-numbers: Open the [Reports screen](1) in the admin and pick 7, 30 or 90 days. It has a "Content used most" list and a "Content never used" list, based on which pages and written answers were given to the assistant to answer visitors. Only visitor answers count, not "Try it" or test runs. You can download the table as CSV.
answers.reference-numbers:

More is on [the Reports page][1].

cases.question: How are visitor questions grouped into topics?

answers.source-numbers:
The answer review names them. When it reviews an answer, it is given the assistant's current topic names and either picks one or proposes a new short label of 2 to 4 words (at most 40 characters, in the language of the question). The topic is stored on the visitor's question, and each question is tagged once.

An assistant can have at most 40 topics, plus "Other". Off-topic questions get no topic, and you cannot tag messages by hand. The grouped list, with the share left unanswered per topic, is on the [Reports](2) screen.
answers.reference-numbers:
The answer review names a topic for each visitor question. It either picks one of the assistant's existing topic names or proposes a new short label of 2 to 4 words, in the language of the question. Each question is tagged once, and there is no manual tagging.

An assistant can have at most 40 topics, plus "Other". Off-topic questions get no topic. Read more on [the topics page][1], and see [Reports][2] for the topic list with counts and the share unanswered.
answers.copied-addresses: Each visitor question gets a short topic label (2 to 4 words) from the answer review, which picks one of the assistant's existing topics or proposes a new one. The label is stored on the visitor's question, and a question is tagged once. An assistant can have at most 40 topics, plus "Other". Questions that are off topic get no topic. See [Topics](https://docs.solv.chat/topics) for more. The [Reports screen](https://docs.solv.chat/reports) lists the topics, most asked first.

cases.question: Is SQLite free to use commercially?

answers.source-numbers:
Yes. SQLite is in the [public domain](2), so you can copy, modify, sell or distribute it for any purpose, commercial or not, without paying royalties. The [FAQ](4) says the same.

If your company wants legal proof of its right to use it, or indemnity, Hwaci sells an optional Warranty of Title. Paid support is also available.
answers.reference-numbers:
Yes. SQLite is in the public domain, so you can use it in a commercial product without paying royalties. [The SQLite FAQ][4] says you can do anything you want with it, and [the copyright page][2] says anyone may copy, modify, sell or distribute it for any purpose.

If your company wants legal proof of its right to use it, for example indemnity against copyright claims, Hwaci sells a Warranty of Title. Paid support is also available, and some extensions to SQLite are proprietary and licensed.
